Demo 10: Mixer — Intelligent Audio Balancing (TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG)

Headline
Implement a behavior-aware Mixer runtime that enforces deterministic mix groups, priority-based ducking/boosting, and voice-limiting using declarative rules stored in repo JSON files.

Problem statement
Under concurrent audio/visual load (footsteps, combat, UI, ambience, etc.) outputs can mask each other and create an unusable, noisy mix. We need a deterministic runtime Mixer that applies intent-aware prioritization, ducking/boosting, and voice limits so the system maintains clarity and intent without human mixing.

Users
- Game/audio integrators and developers who embed ToneForge into interactive systems and need predictable, low-latency arbitration of concurrent outputs.
- Example user stories:
  - As a game audio engineer, I want ambience to be automatically ducked when combat activates so critical sounds remain audible.
  - As a developer, I want per-group voice limits so the system never exceeds allowed concurrent sources and avoids CPU spikes.
  - As an accessibility engineer, I want deterministic rules so we can reliably tune priority behavior and test outcomes.

Success criteria (measurable)
- Mix groups implemented and configurable: footsteps, UI, combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts.
- Voice limiting enforced per group with default max voices = 4; tests confirm group never exceeds limit under load.
- State-driven duck/boost rules applied from declarative JSON; default duck depth = 6 dB and UI duck duration = 200 ms.
- Max end-to-end mixer decision latency ≤ 5 ms under target load (benchmarked in CI test harness).
- `mixer` behavior is deterministic and unit-testable: same input state & events → identical rule outcomes and gains.

Constraints
- Depends on Runtime and State (Demo 9) being available for the Mixer to observe state and for Runtime to apply gain/limits.
- Must be low-latency and deterministic; avoid complex ML inference in the runtime path (Intelligence can suggest rules but must not auto-apply them).
- Rules storage must be auditable and version-controlled in the repository.

Existing state
- PRD: `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` contains an extensive product-level design and examples.
- Roadmap: `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` includes Demo 10 context and example `mixer.inspect()` interactions.
- Worklog: TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG exists (title: "Demo 10: Mixer -- Intelligent Audio Balancing") and currently in `idea` stage, `open` status, assignee `Map`.

Desired change
- Implement core Mixer runtime features:
  - Mix group abstraction (intent-based groups)
  - Priority-based rule engine applying duck/boost/limit actions
  - Voice limiting enforcement per group
  - Deterministic rule evaluation with unit tests and fixtures
- Provide declarative rule schema and example JSON rules stored in `.toneforge/mixer/*.json`.

Related work
- Potentially related docs:
  - `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` — full Mixer PRD describing concepts, examples, and goals.
  - `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — demo sequence and Demo 10 scenario showing expected interactions.
  - `docs/prd/BRAINSTORM_QUESTIONS.md` — design tradeoffs and concerns about Mixer responsibilities.

- Potentially related work items:
  - Demo 10: Mixer -- Intelligent Audio Balancing (TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG) — current work item (idea, open, assignee Map).
  - Demo 13: Visualizer & Haptics -- Cross-Modal Output (TF-0MLXF9O241QG5APK) — lists Demo 10 as a prerequisite; cross-modal alignment may be relevant later.

Notes & open questions
- Rule storage path proposed: `.toneforge/mixer/*.json` (chosen to be versionable and human-editable). Confirm if another location is preferred.
- Scope: this work item covers the core runtime (mix groups, priority/rule engine, voice-limiting, deterministic evaluation). It intentionally excludes CLI/demo scripting and visual intensity control unless requested.

Draft created for review. Please review and either (A) approve, or (B) provide edits/answers to the short clarifying questions below.

Clarifying questions (pick or freeform)
1) Confirm the rules file path: `.toneforge/mixer/*.json`? (Yes / Different path)
2) Confirm mix group list: footsteps, UI, combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts? (Yes / Add/Remove)
3) Do you want me to add Demo 9 (Runtime & State) as a blocking dependency on the work item now, or should we leave dependency recording to a Producer? (Add now / Leave to Producer)

Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Scope creep — implementing cross‑modal visuals, CLI demos, or Intelligence auto‑apply could expand work beyond core runtime. Mitigation: record additional features as separate work items and keep this item focused on core runtime implementation.
- Risk: Runtime/State interfaces change during Demo 9 work, causing rework. Mitigation: lock an interface contract (API surface) in a short integration spike or use feature toggles; coordinate with Demo 9 owners.
- Risk: Real‑time performance targets are missed under heavy load. Mitigation: add microbenchmarks to CI and measure worst‑case latency; implement graceful degradation (looser voice limits) as a fallback.
- Assumption: Rules will be authored as declarative JSON and are sufficient to express required duck/boost/limit logic; more complex decision logic will be suggested by Intelligence but only applied after human review.

Polish
- The proposed canonical rules path is `.toneforge/mixer/*.json` (versionable and human-editable). Example rule schema and a small set of example rules should be added in the first implementation PR.

Final draft: please confirm or provide last edits. Once approved I will remove this temporary draft file and keep the work item updated.

```bash
toneforge intelligence audit --library ./library
```

As a developer preparing for release, I want to validate my sound library against platform-specific quality rules and compile it into optimized, production-ready packages with deterministic build manifests.

```bash
toneforge validate --library ./library --ruleset mobile --strictness warning

toneforge compile --library ./library --target mobile --rules presets/compile/mobile_aggressive.json --output ./dist/mobile/
toneforge compile --library ./library --target web --dry-run
```

- `toneforge validate --library <dir> --ruleset <name> --strictness <level>`
- `toneforge compile --library <dir> --category <c> --target <platform> --rules <file> --output <dir>`
- `toneforge compile --dry-run`

1. Validator checks: peak clipping, duration bounds, silence ratio

3. Compiler produces WAV files + manifest.json for target platform

- Demo 9: Runtime & State -- Real-Time Behavioral Sound (TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1)

Network, Integrations

**Network (two browser windows side by side):**
- Host broadcasts state changes to connected peers
- Client receives state changes and plays deterministically identical audio
- State transitions are synchronized across all connected clients

**Integrations (CI pipeline):**
- Generate, validate, compile, and export sounds in automated pipelines
- Export for Unity/web with platform-appropriate file structure

- `toneforge sync --target <engine> --library <path> --output <path>`
- Network API: `network.host()`, `network.join()`

2. Network bandwidth is under 1 KB/s for typical gameplay
3. CI pipeline validates, compiles, and exports without manual intervention
4. Unity/web export produces platform-appropriate file structure
5. Late-join clients receive state snapshot and sync correctly

# Machine-use demo: JSON-driven reporting batch script

## Problem statement

ToneForge's CLI exposes `--json` on its commands so that machines and agents can
consume structured output, but no demo actually *exercises* that JSON
programmatically. Machine consumption is documented and asserted per-command in
unit tests, yet there is no end-to-end example that proves the JSON is
sufficient to build a real automation workflow (discover items in a category,
reconcile against already-used sounds, produce a report).

## Users

- **AI agents and automation authors** integrating ToneForge into batch
  pipelines, who need a copy-pasteable pattern for consuming `--json` output.
- **Game/application developers and sound designers** selecting new placeholder
  sounds for a project while avoiding reuse of sounds they have already placed.
- **ToneForge maintainers**, who gain a regression guard that the
  `list recipes --json` contract stays stable and parseable by an external
  consumer.

Example user stories:

- As an automation author, I run a reporting script that lists every recipe in a
  chosen category as JSON, removes the ones recorded in my project's
  already-used sounds list, and prints the remaining candidates, so I can pick
  new sounds without manually cross-checking spreadsheets.
- As an agent, I call the same script with `--json` and feed its report into
  further tooling (asset planning, generation queues) without scraping
  human-readable text.
- As a maintainer, I want an automated test that runs the reporting script
  end-to-end, so a breaking change to the `list recipes --json` shape fails CI
  rather than silently breaking downstream consumers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new demo walkthrough `demos/machine-use.md` exists and follows the demo
   markdown convention (`docs`/`demos/README.md` front matter with `title`, `id`,
   `description`; `##` step headings; executable `bash` code blocks; `toneforge`
   as the command name), and its steps form a complete, runnable JSON-driven
   reporting batch-script walkthrough.
2. A reusable reporting script (proposed `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh`)
   exists that:
   (a) obtains the items in a selected category via a `--json` CLI call
   (`toneforge list recipes --category <category> --json`);
   (b) reads a list of already-used sounds from a file;
   (c) filters the used sounds out and emits a report of the remaining
   candidates on stdout — a human-readable summary by default and a structured
   JSON report when the script is invoked with `--json`.
3. The script parses CLI JSON using only tooling already available in the
   project runtime (Node.js); it does not add a new runtime dependency (e.g.
   `jq`) as a hard requirement.
4. The script exits non-zero with a clear diagnostic when its input file is
   missing/malformed or the underlying CLI call fails; an empty result set
   (every category item already used) is a successful outcome (exit 0), not an
   error.
5. An automated test exercises the reporting script end-to-end against a
   committed fixture (a known category + already-used list) and asserts that
   used recipes are excluded, non-used recipes are included, and the `--json`
   report is valid JSON with the expected fields. The test is a regression guard
   on the `list recipes --json` contract.
6. The new demo walkthrough parses cleanly with the existing demo parser
   (`src/demo/parser.ts`), consistent with the other `demos/*.md` walkthroughs.
7. Existing human-readable output is unchanged: running the same commands
   without `--json` still produces the current text output.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Consumer, not a change to the CLI.** This item consumes the existing
  `--json` output; it must not alter CLI behaviour. Any JSON gap discovered
  (missing field, unstable shape) becomes a separate linked work item rather
  than being silently fixed here.
- **No new runtime dependency.** JSON parsing in the script must use Node.js,
  which the project already requires; `jq` may be mentioned only as an optional
  alternative, never a hard prerequisite.
- **Headless and deterministic.** The demo/script must not require audio
  hardware and must produce the same report for the same inputs.
- **Convention-bound.** Follow `demos/README.md` for the walkthrough and the
  existing `scripts/*.sh` style for the script.
- **CHANGELOG.md is out of scope** — it is managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline.

## Existing state

- `src/cli/commands/list.ts` emits, under `--json`:
  `{ command: "list", resource: "recipes", total, recipes: [{ name, description, category, tags }], filters? }`.
  `--category` matches after normalising case, spaces and hyphens.
- `src/cli.runtime.ts` (`library list`) emits
  `{ command: "library list", category?, count, entries: [{ id, recipe, seed, category, duration, tags, promotedAt }] }`.
- Demos are Markdown walkthroughs in `demos/*.md` parsed by `src/demo/parser.ts`
  and run by `scripts/demo/run.ts` (`npm run demo`). `demos/demo-07-library.sh`
  is the one existing bash-script demo and is the closest precedent; it already
  pipes `--json` output through `node -e` JSON parsing.
- `scripts/generate-tableau-example.sh` is the precedent for a standalone,
  reusable `scripts/*.sh` batch script that invokes the `toneforge` CLI.
- `demos/recipe-filtering.md` Act 7 documents `list recipes --json` and states
  the intent to "pipe the `--json` output into a script" — a natural link for
  the new demo, but it does not provide the script itself.
- A `PaletteManifest` (`src/tui/types.ts`) already models a list of chosen
  recipes (`entries[].recipe`), which is a natural structured source of
  "already used sounds".

## Desired change

Add a machine-consumption demo and the reporting batch script it drives:

1. **Reporting script** (proposed `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh`):
   - Resolve the `toneforge` CLI (falling back to `npx --prefix <repo>` like
     `demo-07-library.sh`).
   - Read a category (argument, default e.g. `card-game`) and a used-sounds file
     (argument, with a committed demo fixture as default).
   - Call `toneforge list recipes --category <category> --json` and parse the
     `recipes` array with `node -e`.
   - Select only recipes whose `name` is not present in the used-sounds list.
   - Emit a report: by default a readable summary (category, total, used,
     remaining, and the remaining names); with `--json`, a structured object
     (e.g. `{ command, category, total, used, remaining, candidates: [...] }`).
   - Exit 0 on success (including an empty candidate list) and non-zero with a
     clear message on bad input/CLI failure.
2. **Demo walkthrough** (`demos/machine-use.md`): a short, narrated
   multi-step walkthrough in the established convention that:
   - motivates the problem (choosing new sounds without reusing existing ones);
   - shows the raw `list recipes --category <c> --json` output;
   - runs the reporting script (human-readable, then `--json`);
   - shows how the JSON report composes with further tooling (e.g. a
     generation queue), including a note that human output is unchanged.
3. **Test**: an automated test that seeds a fixture used-sounds file and a
   known category, runs the script, and asserts filtering + JSON validity +
   field presence, guarding the `list recipes --json` contract.
4. **Fixture**: a small committed "already used sounds" sample file used by the
   demo and the test.

## Key Files:

- `demos/machine-use.md` — New demo walkthrough (front matter + `##` steps +
  `bash` blocks) narrating the JSON-driven reporting workflow.
- `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` — New reusable reporting batch script
  that consumes `list recipes --json` and filters a used-sounds list.
- `demos/README.md` / `README.md` — Index/mention the new demo and script.
- `src/demo/parser.ts` — Reference only; the new walkthrough must parse with it.
- `src/cli/commands/list.ts` — Reference only; the `list recipes --json`
  contract the script consumes (change only if a documented gap is found, as a
  separate item).
- `src/cli.runtime.ts` — Reference only; the `library list --json` contract if
  the library route is chosen.
- `scripts/generate-tableau-example.sh`, `demos/demo-07-library.sh` — Style
  precedents for CLI-invoking bash scripts and JSON parsing with `node -e`.
- A test file under `src/` (e.g. `src/demo/machine-use.integration.test.ts`) and
  a fixture used-sounds file — end-to-end regression guard for the JSON contract.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Category/item source ambiguity** — "items in a particular category" could
  mean *recipes* (`list recipes --category`) or *library entries*
  (`library list --category`). **Assumption (recommended default):** recipes,
  because categories are first-class, the set is stable and requires no prior
  `explore promote` step, and it matches the `demos/recipe-filtering.md`
  precedent. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1.
- **Used-sounds list format** — could be plain text (one name per line) or a
  structured `PaletteManifest`/JSON. **Assumption (recommended default):**
  support a plain newline-delimited list by default, with the option to read a
  manifest's `entries[].recipe` later if needed. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q2.
- **Deliverable shape** — script-only vs script + demo walkthrough.
  **Assumption (recommended default):** both, matching the project's
  demo-walkthrough convention and the seed's "new demo" wording. Recorded as
  OPEN QUESTION Q3.
- **Runtime portability** — relying on `node -e` is portable within this repo
  but slightly verbose; a `jq` shortcut would be terser but adds a prerequisite.
  Assumption: Node-only is the safer default.
- **Scope creep** — while building the script, additional `--json` gaps (e.g.
  missing fields, inconsistent `command` values) may surface. These must be
  recorded as separate linked work items, not folded into this one.
- **Exit-code semantics** — "zero remaining candidates" must be treated as
  success; conflating it with "no matches = error" would break CI usage.

## Related work

- **TF-0MLYO1Y3S0E43PA7** — Add json output (completed; discovered-from). The
  feature this demo exercises; defines the per-command JSON contract.
  (children: TF-0MLYUBYAI15BNLGJ, TF-0MLYUBZZP1HR08I8, TF-0MLYUC2W71V28AKZ,
  TF-0MLYUC5UW1L88ZHB, TF-0MLYUC8WF03NYR3P).
- **TF-0MM87IJAY06JSWI7** — Demo: Recipe Filtering (completed). Documents
  `list recipes --json` (Act 7) and states the pipe-into-a-script intent; this
  demo delivers the missing script.
- **TF-0MM1GPMFF0HCCJHS** — Library Walkthrough -- Demo Script (completed).
  Closest bash-script demo precedent (`demos/demo-07-library.sh`).
- **TF-0MLYG5SUM0F6C40K** — Batch Generation Demo Walkthrough (completed).
  Precedent for a batch-oriented walkthrough.
- **TF-0MM7HULM506CGSOP** — TUI Wizard: Interactive Sound Palette Builder
  (completed). Owns the `PaletteManifest`, the closest existing structured
  "selected sounds" model.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **TF-0MMMATPB20DLIA1Z** – Isolate CLI integration tests via child-process spawning (completed)
- **TF-0MM4M1EID1OCLM3Y** – Remove runtime demo and CLI command (completed)
- **TF-0MUUPAQ7U008H26I** – Make node-web-audio-api optional in package.json (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_10_05.md` — matched: already, category, cli, commands, content (+16 more)
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — matched: already, category, cli, commands, content (+13 more)
- `demos/sound-creation.md` — matched: already, category, cli, create, filtering (+11 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION Q1 (which "items in a particular category"):** Should the
  reporting script discover **recipes** via
  `toneforge list recipes --category <c> --json`, or **library entries** via
  `toneforge library list --category <c> --json`? **Recommended:** recipes —
  categories are first-class and stable, no prior `explore promote` step is
  needed, and it matches the existing `demos/recipe-filtering.md` JSON
  precedent. No blocking answer required; the recommendation is the documented
  default for implementation. Source: interactive reply pending (producer
  review requested).
- **OPEN QUESTION Q2 (already-used list format):** Should the already-used
  sounds be supplied as a plain newline-delimited text file, as a JSON
  `PaletteManifest` (`entries[].recipe`), or both? **Recommended:** plain
  newline-delimited list by default (simplest, language-agnostic, easy to
  hand-edit), with manifest support considered only if the producer wants it.
  Source: interactive reply pending (producer review requested).
- **OPEN QUESTION Q3 (deliverable shape):** Should this item deliver (a) only a
  standalone reporting script under `scripts/`, (b) only a demo walkthrough in
  `demos/`, or (c) both? **Recommended:** (c) both — the seed asks for "a new
  demo", and the project convention is a Markdown walkthrough, while the
  reporting batch script is the reusable artefact. Source: interactive reply
  pending (producer review requested).

# Realtime adjustment of parameters — Intake Brief

## Headline

Allow continuous/looping sounds (initially vehicle engines) to have their parameters
modulated during playback, via the Runtime API defined in `RUNTIME_PRD.md`.

## Problem statement

Some sounds — engine noise being the motivating example — need to vary while they play
(pitch/RPM, filter, intensity) rather than being fixed at trigger time. The Runtime
currently exposes per-event parameters only; there is no way to change a parameter of a
sound that is already playing.

## Users

- Game developers who need engine/loop sounds to respond continuously to gameplay state
  (RPM, load, speed).
- Example user stories:
  - As a game audio developer, I want an engine loop's pitch to track RPM while it
    plays, so the sound feels connected to the vehicle.
  - As a developer, I want to set a named parameter on a playing sound, so I can
    modulate it from game logic without restarting it.
  - As a maintainer, I want parameter changes to remain deterministic, so playback stays
    reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `setSfxParameter(id, name, value)` (per `RUNTIME_PRD.md` §6) updates a parameter of a
   currently playing sound in real time; the first supported scope is continuous/looping
   sounds only.
2. Engine-style pitch/RPM modulation is supported, consistent with `CORE_PRD.md` §6.5
   (loop + oscillator/LFO pitch modulation).
3. Parameter changes are deterministic: a given seed and ordered sequence of parameter
   events produce identical output.
4. Invalid parameter names or out-of-range values are rejected with actionable errors
   and do not corrupt playback state.
5. Unit tests cover successful modulation, determinism, and invalid-input handling, plus
   at least one demonstrable engine-style user story.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is limited to focused continuous-sound parameter modulation (producer decision,
  parent Appendix Q3). General real-time parameter automation for arbitrary sounds is a
  documented future extension (`RUNTIME_PRD.md` §16) and out of scope.
- Must not break existing Node or browser workflows.

## Existing state

- `RUNTIME_PRD.md` §4.1 lists "optional parameter overrides"; §6 defines
  `setSfxParameter(id, "intensity", 0.5)`; §16 lists "Runtime parameter automation" as
  a future extension.
- `CORE_PRD.md` §6.5 designs vehicle engines as a looping sample with LFO pitch
  modulation.
- `src/runtime/` orchestrates state/context/sequences; runtime audio playback wiring is
  being addressed separately by TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ and TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0.

## Desired change

- Implement `setSfxParameter` on the Runtime, scoped to continuous/looping sounds.
- Expose it through the public runtime API and cover it with tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/runtime/runtime.ts` — add `setSfxParameter`/parameter state.
- `src/runtime/index.ts` — export the new API surface.
- `src/runtime/runtime.test.ts` — modulation and determinism tests.
- `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md` — confirm/adjust the parameter API description.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** depends on runtime→audio playback wiring that is still in flight.
  *Mitigation:* implement against the Runtime API surface and keep it backend-agnostic;
  record a possible blocking relationship with TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ.
- **Risk:** scope creep into general automation. *Mitigation:* limit to continuous
  sounds; defer general automation to a future item.
- **Assumption:** `setSfxParameter` is the agreed API name (from `RUNTIME_PRD.md` §6).

## Related work

# Mixer runtime foundation — Intake Brief

## Headline

Implement the deterministic core Mixer runtime for Demo 10: MixGroup metadata,
active-voice tracking, and declarative rule evaluation that emits duck/boost/limit
decisions per event.

## Problem statement

Under concurrent load (footsteps, combat, UI, ambience, etc.) sound sources mask each
other and produce an unclear, fatiguing mix. The runtime needs a deterministic
arbitration layer that applies intent-aware prioritisation, ducking/boosting and voice
limiting so the mix stays clear without human intervention.

## Users

- Game/audio integrators embedding ToneForge who need predictable, low-latency
  arbitration of concurrent outputs.
- Example user stories:
  - As a game audio engineer, I want ambience automatically ducked when combat
    activates, so critical sounds stay audible.
  - As a developer, I want per-group voice limits, so the system never exceeds allowed
    concurrent sources and avoids CPU spikes.
  - As an accessibility engineer, I want deterministic rules, so priority behaviour can
    be tuned and tested reliably.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `MixGroup` metadata (name, priority, `maxVoices` default 4, current gain) is defined
   for the six confirmed groups: footsteps, UI, combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts.
2. Active voices are tracked per group; a group never admits or reports more voices
   than its `maxVoices` limit, under simulated load.
3. Declarative rules (`when {state|context}` → `then {duck|boost|limit}`) are evaluated
   to produce per-event decisions, with default duck depth 6 dB and UI duck duration
   200 ms.
4. Rule evaluation is deterministic: identical input state and events produce identical
   outcomes and gains, verified by unit tests.
5. Rule evaluation is constant-time per event and adds ≤ 5 ms end-to-end decision
   latency under the target load, verified by a CI benchmark.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Depends on Demo 9 Runtime & State (completed) and the Mixer rule config loader
  (TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594).
- No ML inference in the runtime path; Intelligence may suggest rules but must never
  auto-apply them.
- Must remain low-latency and deterministic.

## Existing state

- `src/runtime/` orchestrates state/context/sequence presets but produces no audio.
- `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` §4–7 defines mix groups, priority, declarative rules and the
  `mixer.applyRules()` API.
- Mixer rules are stored under `.toneforge/mixer/*.json` (confirmed, parent Appendix
  Q2.1); the loader is delivered by TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594.

## Desired change

- Add a Mixer core module (types + runtime) under `src/mixer/` implementing the group
  registry, voice ledger, and rule evaluation.
- Expose a small API for the Runtime/State layer to update state and read mix
  decisions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/mixer/types.ts` — MixGroup, voice and decision types.
- `src/mixer/runtime.ts` — group registry, voice tracking, rule evaluation.
- `src/mixer/__tests__/runtime.test.ts` — determinism and latency tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Demo 9 / Runtime interfaces change, causing rework. *Mitigation:* keep the
  Mixer API narrow and covered by contract tests.
- **Risk:** performance target missed under heavy load. *Mitigation:* CI microbenchmark
  plus graceful degradation of voice limits.
- **Assumption:** rules are purely declarative and sufficient for duck/boost/limit;
  complex decisions remain human-approved suggestions from Intelligence.
- **Scope-creep note:** CLI/demo scripting, visual intensity and cross-modal output are
  out of scope — record them as separate work items.

## Related work

- `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` — Mixer concepts, rules and API.
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` (Demo 10) — expected `mixer.inspect()` interaction.

# Mixer rule config loader — Intake Brief

## Headline

Define the declarative Mixer rule schema and implement a validating loader for
`.toneforge/mixer/*.json`, exposing validated rule sets to the Mixer runtime.

## Problem statement

The Mixer runtime needs auditable, version-controlled rules to drive duck/boost/limit
decisions, but no schema or loader exists. Without validation, a malformed rule file
would silently change or break mix behaviour at runtime.

## Users

- Game/audio engineers tuning mix behaviour via human-editable rules.
- Maintainers who need rule files version-controlled and validated in CI.
- Example user stories:
  - As an audio engineer, I want to edit a JSON rule and have the Mixer apply it
    deterministically, so I can tune behaviour without code changes.
  - As a developer, I want malformed rules rejected with actionable errors, so bad
    config never reaches runtime.
  - As a maintainer, I want rules version-controlled under `.toneforge/mixer/`, so
    changes are reviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented rule schema covers `duck`, `boost`, `limit` actions and
   state/context triggers (`when {state|context}` → `then {...}`), including the six
   mix groups and defaults (`maxVoices` 4, duck depth 6 dB, UI duck duration 200 ms).
2. The loader reads rules from `.toneforge/mixer/*.json` (confirmed path), falling back
   to built-in defaults when absent — consistent with the `.toneforge/config.yaml`
   fallback in `src/classify/dimensions/category.ts`.
3. Invalid rules are rejected with actionable validation errors; valid rule sets are
   exposed to the runtime.
4. A seed/example rules file is committed under `.toneforge/mixer/`.
5. Unit tests cover loading, defaults when absent, and validation failures.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Rules must be deterministic, auditable and version-controlled.
- Schema must not require dynamic code execution; JSON only.
- Path is fixed at `.toneforge/mixer/` per producer decision (parent Appendix Q2.1).

## Existing state

- No `config/` directory exists; content presets live under `presets/{recipes,sequences,stacks}`.
- Project config convention is `.toneforge/config.yaml` (`src/classify/dimensions/category.ts`).
- `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` §4.3 shows the intended rule shape
  (`{ "when": {"state": "combat"}, "then": {"duck": [...], "boost": [...], "limit": [...]} }`).

## Desired change

- Add a schema module and a loader under `src/mixer/` (e.g. `schema.ts`,
  `rules-loader.ts`).
- Commit a seed rules file and wire the loader into the Mixer runtime.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.toneforge/mixer/rules.json` — seed/example declarative rules.
- `src/mixer/schema.ts` — rule schema and validation.
- `src/mixer/rules-loader.ts` — load + defaults + validation entry point.
- `src/mixer/__tests__/rules-loader.test.ts` — load/defaults/validation tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** rules schema churns as the runtime firms up. *Mitigation:* keep the schema

- **Risk:** silent fallback to defaults masks a broken rule file. *Mitigation:* warn

# Mixer voice limiting tests — Intake Brief

## Headline

Add deterministic tests proving the Mixer enforces per-group voice limits and applies
the default duck/boost/limit rules for all six mix groups.

## Problem statement

Voice limiting and rule outcomes are the safety-critical behaviour of the Mixer: if a
group can exceed its voice limit, or rules are non-deterministic, mixes break under
load and become untestable. These behaviours need explicit regression coverage.

## Users

- Mixer/runtime developers who need fast, deterministic feedback on rule changes.
- Maintainers who need a regression guard that voice limits and default rule outcomes
  cannot silently change.
- Example user stories:
  - As a developer, I want a test that fails if a group ever exceeds its voice limit,
    so the safety property is enforced.
  - As a maintainer, I want fixture-based rule tests, so default behaviour is
    documented and stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Tests assert the default `maxVoices` of 4 per group and prove a group never exceeds
   its limit under simulated load.
2. Fixtures verify default duck/boost/limit outcomes for all six groups: footsteps, UI,
   combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts.
3. Tests verify the state-driven combat rule (ambience ducked −6 dB, combat boosted)
   and the UI duck defaults (6 dB, 200 ms).
4. Determinism: fixed seed/state fixtures produce byte-stable outcomes across repeated
   runs.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Tests must be deterministic (no wall-clock or load-order dependence) and fast.

## Summary

Create a thin cross-platform audio abstraction module that provides `OfflineAudioContext` and `AudioContext` types/APIs usable in both Node.js (via `node-web-audio-api`) and browser (via native Web Audio API).

## Problem

Both `src/core/renderer.ts` and `src/recipes/index.ts` import `OfflineAudioContext` directly from `node-web-audio-api`, which fails in browser environments. The `sample-loader.ts` already has a working pattern for runtime detection.

## Implementation

1. Create `src/audio/web-audio.ts` that exports:
   - `OfflineAudioContext` — the `OfflineAudioContext` class (from `node-web-audio-api` in Node, global in browser)
   - `AudioContext` — the `AudioContext` class (for real-time playback)
   - `isNodeRuntime()` — runtime detection helper (borrow from `src/core/recipe.ts`)
   - `getAudioContext()` — factory returning a new `AudioContext` (real-time)

2. Use dynamic imports for the Node.js path to avoid browser bundler complaints about `node-web-audio-api`.

3. Update all consumers to import from this module instead of directly from `node-web-audio-api`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/audio/web-audio.ts` exports `OfflineAudioContext`, `AudioContext`, and `isNodeRuntime()`
2. No top-level import of `node-web-audio-api` in `src/core/renderer.ts` or `src/recipes/index.ts`
3. TypeScript compiles without errors
4. All existing tests pass
5. Web build (`npm run build --prefix web`) still succeeds

## Summary

Make the shared render path preset-aware: given a `SoundPreset` (recipe + seed + overrides), render the sound deterministically in the browser via the cross-platform audio abstraction, with overrides replacing seed-derived parameter values. Reuse the existing `buildOfflineGraph`/recipe registry — no duplicated synthesis logic. This is the highest-risk item because today `buildOfflineGraph(rng, ctx, duration)` derives parameters internally and exposes no injection point.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `renderPreset(preset)` entry point returns the same `RenderResult` shape as `renderRecipe` and applies every override in the preset to the rendered audio.
- Determinism: rendering the same `SoundPreset` twice yields byte-identical `Float32Array` samples; changing an override yields *different* samples for at least one representative recipe (both asserted by test).
- Every registered recipe (built-in and file-backed) honours overrides for all of its declared parameters, verified by a registry-wide test that iterates `registry.list()` and asserts an override changes the output.
- Rendering uses the cross-platform Web Audio abstraction (native `OfflineAudioContext` in the browser, `node-web-audio-api` in Node) and imports no Node-only audio module on the browser path.
- Baseline behaviour is unchanged: with no overrides, `renderPreset({recipe, seed, overrides:{}})` is byte-identical to `renderRecipe(recipe, seed)`.
- `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a small `applyOverrides(params, overrides)` helper and thread an optional `overrides` argument through the render path and `RecipeRegistration.buildOfflineGraph` (or an equivalent params-injection hook) — decide the exact seam during the prototype below.
- Refactor built-in recipe graph builders to merge `getParams(rng)` with `overrides`; extend the file-backed registration's existing param-injection to apply overrides.
- Add `renderPreset(preset, duration?)` alongside `renderRecipe` reusing `renderer.ts`; do not fork synthesis.
- Build on the browser-compatible abstraction from TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0 (cross-platform `OfflineAudioContext`/`AudioContext`).

## Prototype / Experiment

Prototype the override seam on 2–3 representative recipes (oscillator, noise/filter, file-backed) before touching all recipes. Success threshold: the representative set renders deterministically and an override demonstrably changes output; then roll the seam out registry-wide behind the registry-wide coverage test.

## Risky assumptions / OPEN QUESTION

**OPEN QUESTION (for producer/architect):** the current `buildOfflineGraph(rng, ctx, duration)` API has no parameter-injection point, and ~60 built-in recipes derive params inside their closure. Preferred approach here is to add an optional `overrides` argument and a tiny merge helper, refactoring recipes mechanically. # Intake Brief: Allow external tools to register recipes via CLI (persistent / external directory)

## Problem statement

The `tf library add` command (completed in TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18) registers recipes only into an in-process `RecipeRegistry` instance. When a separate process runs `tf generate --recipe <name>`, the externally-registered recipe is not discoverable — persistence was explicitly deferred. This blocks build pipelines (e.g. AI_Hell's game SFX workflow) that run `tf library add` and `tf generate` as separate process invocations.

## Users

- **Game audio pipeline (AI_Hell):** Run `tf library add --file ./game-weapon.yaml` from their game repo, then later invoke `tf generate --recipe game-weapon` as part of a deterministic WAV build. They need the recipe to survive across separate process invocations without editing the ToneForge repo.
- **Plugin/tool authors:** Want to ship ToneGraph recipe files alongside their tool and register them for use without modifying ToneForge's source tree.
- **ToneForge CLI users:** Want to organise external recipes in a known location (`~/.toneforge/recipes/`) and have them listed alongside baked-in recipes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Persistent registration:** `tf library add --file <path>` copies the recipe file into a persistent external directory (`~/.toneforge/recipes/` by default), and a subsequent, separate `tf generate --recipe <name>` process discovers and renders the registered recipe.
2. **Custom destination:** `tf library add --file <path> --destination <dir>` stores the recipe in a custom directory. The default directory is configurable via the `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` environment variable.
3. **Idempotent registration:** Registering the same recipe file twice does not error or create duplicates; re-registration is a clean no-op or overwrite.
4. **Validation and error handling:** Invalid recipe files (non-ToneGraph, schema-violating, or corrupt) are rejected with a clear, non-zero-exit error message; the registry/library is left unchanged.
5. **External location isolation:** Registered recipes live outside the ToneForge repo; no editing of repo files is required.
6. **Path resolution:** Both relative and absolute paths are supported for `--file`, `--destination`, and `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR`; path resolution is documented.
7. **External recipes listed:** `tf library list` shows externally registered recipes with their source directory, alongside baked-in recipes.
8. **Test suite passes:** `npm test` passes with the new changes.
9. **Help documentation:** CLI help output documents the new/updated commands with at least one worked example.

## Constraints

- ToneForge v0.1.0 — must not break existing `library add` (in-process) behaviour for callers that do not use persistent registration.
- Must remain backwards-compatible with the baked-asset workflow.
- No new Node-only dependency in the browser runtime bundle (Node fs/path imports must be guarded by runtime detection, per the pattern in `src/core/recipe.ts`).
- The persistent directory is platform-agnostic (`~/.toneforge/` using the OS home directory).
- `initializeRecipeRegistry()` must continue to work in browser environments (discovery is a no-op when not in Node).

## Existing state

- `tf library add` (TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18) registers a recipe into the in-process `RecipeRegistry` but does not persist to disk.
- `discoverFileBackedRecipes()` in `src/core/recipe.ts` is already parameterised with `options.recipeDirectory` but is called with no options from `initializeRecipeRegistry()`, always using the hardcoded `presets/recipes/` directory.
- `presets/recipes/` contains the baked-in YAML recipes (e.g. `weapon-laser-zap.yaml`).
- `isNodeRuntime()` guard pattern exists in `src/core/recipe.ts` for runtime detection.

## Desired change

- Enhance `tf library add` to persist recipe files to a configurable external directory.
- Wire the persistent directory into `discoverFileBackedRecipes()` via `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` env var or `--destination` flag.
- Update `tf library list` to surface externally registered recipes.
- Ensure `initializeRecipeRegistry()` discovers recipes from both the baked-in directory and the persistent/external directory(s).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli/commands/library.ts` — update `add` subcommand to support `--destination`
- `src/cli.runtime.ts` — dispatch logic for `library add` with persistent storage; update `library list` to show external recipes
- `src/core/recipe.ts` — `discoverFileBackedRecipes()` to accept multiple directories (persistent + baked); update `initializeRecipeRegistry()` to pass the persistent directory
- `src/recipes/index.ts` — `initializeRecipeRegistry()` to resolve and pass the persistent directory
- `package.json` / `tsconfig.json` — no changes expected (fs/path are Node built-ins)

## Chosen mechanism

**Hybrid of (A) persistent `library add` + (B) `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` env var.**

`tf library add --file <path>` copies the recipe into `~/.toneforge/recipes/` (configurable via `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR`). The `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` directory is discovered alongside `presets/recipes/` during `initializeRecipeRegistry()`, so any `tf generate` process will find the externally registered recipe. An optional `--destination <dir>` flag overrides the default for a single operation.

This approach:
- Extends the existing `library add` command (backward-compatible)
- Creates a discoverable, persistent external location
- Supports multiple recipes from the same directory
- Works with fresh `tf generate` process invocations (the key requirement)
- `tf library list` can enumerate the persistent directory and mark entries as "external"

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Adding `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` may invite requests for multiple directories, a full config file, or per-project discovery paths. Scope is one directory env var + `--destination` for single operations.
- **Browser compatibility:** Persistent directory discovery must be guarded by `isNodeRuntime()` — same pattern already used for `presets/recipes/`.
- **Concurrent writes:** If two processes call `library add` simultaneously, file writes should be atomic (write to temp, then rename).
- **Migration risk:** Existing `library add` callers are unaffected; the change is purely additive.

## Related work

- **TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18** — Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes (completed, superseded the persistence scope)
- **TF-0MUV8YKFR002BIA2** — Add frequency-ramp (sweep) support to ToneGraph for file-backed recipes (related enhancement)
- **AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51** — Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AI_Hell consumer; blocks on this)
- **AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD** — Deterministic WAV build pipeline (AI_Hell consumer; blocks on this)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which mechanism should be chosen for external recipe registration? (A) Persist `library add`, (B) `--recipe-dir` flag, or (C) `--recipe-file` flag? — **Answer (Map):** Hybrid of (A) + (B). `tf library add --file <path>` persists to `~/.toneforge/recipes/` (configurable via `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR`). The persistent directory is discovered alongside baked-in recipes. This satisfies the requirement that a *separate* `tf generate` process discovers the recipe. Rationale: the existing `library add` command (TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18) was designed for registration but deferred persistence; extending it is the minimal, backward-compatible change. The `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` env var provides the script-friendly configurability that (B) would offer. Source: codebase inspection of `src/core/recipe.ts`, `src/recipes/index.ts`, `src/cli/commands/library.ts`.

## Goal

Stop the CLI integration test for malformed presets from writing into the shared
`presets/sequences/` directory, so a leaked or in-flight fixture can never make
unrelated tests fail and turn a full `npm test` run red.

## Context (discovered-from: TF-0MUWK92C10094X5I)

Found while investigating the auto-created test-failure item
TF-0MUWK92C10094X5I ("<suite exited 1>: npm --silent test"). That item was
concurrently closed as a false blocker and attributed to a `node-web-audio-api`
`startRendering()` flake. This is a **separate, independently reproducible**
suite-failure mechanism that is not yet tracked.

## Root cause

`src/cli.yargs.integration.test.ts` ("returns non-zero for a malformed preset
file") writes a malformed fixture directly into the shared, repo-tracked preset
directory:

    join(PROJECT_ROOT, "presets", "sequences", "__malformed_test__.json")

and removes it in a `finally` block.

Other test files discover and parse **every** `.json` in that same directory:

- `src/sequence/golden-fixtures.test.ts` (`discoverPresets()` → `readdirSync(PRESETS_DIR)`)
  registers 3 `it.each` tests per discovered file.
- `src/cli.yargs.integration.test.ts` itself has `list sequences --json` tests
  that expect exit code 0.

Consequences:

1. **In-flight race (parallel workers):** while the malformed test is running,
   any concurrently-executing test that reads `presets/sequences/` sees the
   invalid JSON and fails.
2. **Persistent poisoning (killed run):** if a run is interrupted/timed out
   (e.g. the test-skill timeout or a SIGKILL) the `finally` cleanup never runs,
   leaving `__malformed_test__.json` on disk. Every later full run then fails
   `golden-fixtures` deterministically. The file is **not** covered by
   `.gitignore`, so it is also an accidentally-committable untracked artefact.

This matches the observed signature: a leaked `presets/sequences/__malformed_test__.json`
was present in `git status` at the start of the TF-0MUWK92C10094X5I session.

## Reproduction / evidence

With the leaked fixture present:

    printf '{ this is not valid json' > presets/sequences/__malformed_test__.json
    npx vitest run src/sequence/golden-fixtures.test.ts

Result (deterministic):

    Test Files  1 failed (1)
         Tests  3 failed | 84 passed (87)
    Error: Failed to parse sequence preset '.../presets/sequences/__malformed_test__.json'

The 3 failures are exactly the `it.each` cases for `__malformed_test__.json`
(timeline, 10-run audio determinism, 10-run simulation determinism) — i.e. a
full-suite `Test Files failed` / exit code 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The malformed-preset integration test no longer writes any file into the
   shared repo `presets/sequences/` (or `presets/stacks/`) directory; the
   malformed fixture is created only in an isolated temporary directory that the
   CLI is pointed at.
2. A stray/leaked `presets/sequences/*.json` fixture cannot cause unrelated
   tests (`golden-fixtures.test.ts`, `list sequences` success tests) to fail.
3. Regression coverage proves the isolation — e.g. the malformed-file path is
   detected in a temp directory, and `golden-fixtures` discovery ignores
   test-fixture artefacts — asserting observable behaviour, not source text.
4. Full project test suite passes (`/skill:test`, `--type full`).
5. Any documented behaviour added (e.g. a directory override) is documented;
   when no documented behaviour changes, the completion comment records
   documentation as not applicable.

## Suggested approach

Give the `list sequences` / `list stacks` command an explicit directory source
(e.g. a `--dir <path>` option and/or a `TONEFORGE_SEQUENCES_DIR` /
`TONEFORGE_STACKS_DIR` environment override, mirroring the existing
`TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` pattern in `src/core/recipe.ts`). The malformed test then
creates its fixture in a `tmpdir()` and passes that directory to the CLI,
removing the shared-directory write entirely. Add a defensive filter so
`golden-fixtures` discovery skips `__`-prefixed test artefacts.

## References

- `src/cli.yargs.integration.test.ts` — malformed-preset test (line ~331)
- `src/cli/commands/list.ts` — hardcoded `RESOURCE_DIR` + `listPresets()`
- `src/sequence/golden-fixtures.test.ts` — shared-directory discovery
- `src/core/recipe.ts` — existing `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` directory-override pattern
- Related closed item: TF-0MUWK92C10094X5I
- Related follow-up (different root cause): TF-0MUWLQ8SS0006C9J
